markets: Sells monitoring services to US cardiologists and clinics; no large overseas operations are verified.
rationale: Small US medtech with limited marketing resources; weak F1 fit. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: AOptix Technologies
desc: Developer of iris recognition and identity verification systems using adaptive optics, sold to governments and defence customers.
markets: Sold identity systems to government and defence buyers; current operating status is unclear.
rationale: Possibly inactive government-focused technology firm; no consumer brand, so weak F1 fit.

name: Taikang Bybo Dental
desc: Chinese dental clinic group, affiliated with Taikang Insurance Group, offering general dentistry, implants and orthodontics.
markets: Clinics in China; customers are dental patients; no overseas operations or ownership details are confirmed.
rationale: China-only dental clinic group with limited brand reach; weak F1 fit. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: Aidite
desc: Chinese manufacturer of dental materials such as zirconia blocks and CAD/CAM milling materials for dental laboratories and prosthesis makers.
markets: Sells to dental labs mainly in China; export sales are not verified.
rationale: B2B dental materials supplier with little consumer profile; weak F1 fit. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: Paradigm Spine
desc: Medical device company behind the Coflex interlaminar implant, a motion-preserving alternative to spinal fusion for lumbar stenosis.
markets: Sold Coflex implants to surgeons in the US and Europe; later acquired by RTI Surgical.
rationale: Acquired and absorbed with no independent brand marketing; no F1 relevance. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: Zwipe
desc: Norwegian company making fingerprint-sensing payment and access cards sold to card manufacturers, banks and payment firms.
markets: Customers are card manufacturers and payment companies in Europe, Asia and other regions.
rationale: Payments technology supplier that could showcase biometric cards to banks and card makers; budget is small.

name: CUBOX
desc: Seoul-based company tagged biometrics and information technology in Crunchbase; its products are not confirmed.
markets: Seoul-based; no customers, products or overseas operations are confirmed from the data given.
rationale: Little is known about the business; no evidence of consumer marketing, so F1 fit appears weak.

name: Jiahong DentalLab
desc: Shenzhen dental laboratory company that appears to make dental restorations for dentists; details are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Shenzhen; customers appear to be Chinese dental clinics; no overseas operations are confirmed.
rationale: Dental laboratory with little consumer profile; weak F1 fit. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: DaVita
desc: US provider of kidney care, operating about 3,000 outpatient dialysis centres and integrated kidney care services for patients.
markets: Dialysis centres mainly in the US, plus clinics in about a dozen other countries.
rationale: Large healthcare services brand, but patient services and regulation limit marketing; F1 fit is modest.

name: Target Hospitality
desc: US specialty rental and hospitality services company operating large workforce lodging communities for energy, mining and government customers.
markets: Workforce lodging sites in the US; customers are energy, mining and government clients.
rationale: B2B lodging provider with US-only operations; limited reason to use F1. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: The Clorox Company
desc: US consumer products maker with brands including Clorox bleach and disinfecting wipes, Brita, Glad and Burt's Bees.
markets: Sells in North America, Latin America and other markets, with most sales in the US.
rationale: Household brand owner with consumer marketing budgets; F1 could build awareness, though sales are US-centred.

name: Alcon
desc: Swiss-American eye care company making surgical devices and intraocular lenses plus contact lenses and eye drops.
markets: Sells surgical and vision care products in about 140 countries across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Global eye-care brand that could use F1 for visibility and hospitality with eye surgeons and distributors.

name: AdaptHealth
desc: US provider of home medical equipment and supplies, including sleep apnoea, diabetes, mobility and respiratory products.
markets: Serves patients and referring doctors across the US.
rationale: US-only healthcare supplier with limited consumer brand marketing; weak F1 fit. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: Cencora
desc: US pharmaceutical distributor and health services company supplying drugs and specialty products to pharmacies, hospitals and clinics.
markets: Distributes drugs mainly in the US, with operations in Europe, Canada and Latin America.
rationale: B2B distributor with little consumer brand; F1 offers hospitality for pharma clients, but marketing is limited.
changed: Renamed from AmerisourceBergen to Cencora in 2023

name: Devoted Health
desc: US Medicare Advantage health plan for seniors, with care teams, local clinics and concierge-style member support.
markets: Plans sold to seniors in several US states.
rationale: US-only health plan for seniors; limited alignment with F1 audiences. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: McKesson Medical-Surgical
desc: US distributor of medical supplies, equipment and pharmaceuticals to physician offices, surgery centres and long-term care providers.
markets: Customers are US physician offices, surgery centres and care providers; part of McKesson.
rationale: Segment of a larger distributor with no separate brand marketing; weak F1 fit.

name: Medical Properties Trust
desc: US real estate investment trust owning hospitals and healthcare facilities leased to operators in the US, Europe and Australia.
markets: Properties in the US, UK, Germany and other countries, leased to hospital operators.
rationale: Landlord to hospital operators with no consumer brand; F1 has limited commercial logic.

name: Sound Physicians
desc: US physician services organisation providing hospitalists, critical care, emergency medicine and transitions-of-care programmes under contract to hospitals.
markets: Contracts with US hospitals and health systems; patients are served inside partner hospitals.
rationale: B2B physician staffing group with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: Sotera Health
desc: Provider of sterilisation, lab testing and ionising technologies services for medical device, pharmaceutical and food safety industries.
markets: Operates Sterigenics, Nordion and Nelson Labs sites in North America, Europe and Asia serving manufacturers.
rationale: B2B services group with no consumer brand; F1 fit is limited to client hospitality.

name: Boston Scientific
desc: Medical device maker with products in cardiology, urology, endoscopy and neuromodulation, such as stents, catheters and the Watchman device.
markets: Sells devices to hospitals across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global medtech brand that could use F1 for B2B hospitality with hospitals and a technology showcase.

name: Bausch + Lomb
desc: Eye health company making contact lenses, lens care solutions, eye drops, surgical equipment and prescription ophthalmic products.
markets: Sells eye care products in about 100 countries across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Global eye-care brand with consumer and professional lines; F1 offers visibility and hospitality, though healthcare marketing rules apply.

name: Community Health Systems
desc: US operator of acute-care hospitals and outpatient facilities, running about 70 hospitals in roughly 15 states.
markets: Hospitals in US states only; customers are patients and insurers.
rationale: US hospital chain with regional brands; limited reason to use F1. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: CVS Health
desc: US health care group running CVS Pharmacy stores, the Aetna insurer, Caremark pharmacy benefit manager and Oak Street Health clinics.
markets: Customers are tens of millions of US patients and members; operations are essentially US-only.
rationale: Big US consumer brand, but domestic only; F1 could add hospitality and awareness, though international value is low.

name: emeis
desc: French operator of nursing homes, rehabilitation and psychiatric clinics and home care, with about 1,000 facilities in over 20 countries.
markets: Facilities in Europe, China and Latin America; restructured after the 2022 scandal and financial rescue.
rationale: Care operator with reputation rebuilding but a patient-services model; F1 fit is weak.
changed: Renamed from Orpea to emeis in 2024 after financial restructuring

name: Global Medical Response
desc: US emergency medical services company operating air medical services through Air Methods and ground ambulance through American Medical Response.
markets: Services across the US; customers are patients, hospitals and insurers.
rationale: US-only emergency services provider; limited reason to use F1. The commercial case for an F1 partnership is weak.

name: R1 RCM
desc: US revenue cycle management company that handles patient billing, claims and collections for hospitals and physician groups.
markets: Customers are US hospitals and physician groups, with operations including delivery centres in India.
rationale: B2B service provider with no consumer brand; F1 relevance limited to client hospitality.
changed: Taken private in 2024 by TowerBrook Capital Partners and Clayton, Dubilier & Rice
